domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Match denominators
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or more fractional parts as equivalent fractions so subtraction can be performed with like denominators.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD, LCM, or common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions with the same denominator.
Tag for unlike-denominator subtraction in standalone fractions or in the fractional parts of mixed numbers.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag subtraction of numerators after common denominators are already established.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as n + 0/d or normalizing a nonstandard mixed number unless the step also performs denominator matching.

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number, mixed number, or nonstandard mixed number into an equivalent subtraction-ready form, such as adding a zero fractional part, converting an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number, or converting a mixed number to an improper fraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus a zero fraction, such as 3 = 3 + 0/5.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is normalized to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a mixed number is converted to an improper fraction as the chosen setup for subtraction.
Tag when the purpose of the step is to make operand structure explicit or subtraction-ready before the main subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary separation of already-standard whole and fractional parts if no rewriting occurs.
Do not tag common-denominator conversion alone; that belongs to matching denominators.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the operands are in compatible form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts and fractional parts of mixed numbers are subtracted directly.
Tag when subtraction is performed after normalization or denominator matching, including intermediate negative fractional results before regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or rewriting operands.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping steps that adjust the minuend before subtraction continues.
Do not tag simplification or final recombination alone.

skills.name: Borrow across parts
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as an equivalent fraction and adjust the whole part when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract directly.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly borrows 1 from the whole part.
Tag when 1 whole is rewritten as d/d or equivalent fractional units and added to the fractional part.
Tag when regrouping is used in mixed-number subtraction or whole-minus-fraction subtraction to resolve a negative fractional difference.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag direct subtraction cases that do not require regrouping.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as n + 0/d before any need to borrow; that belongs to operand normalization.
Do not tag final combining or simplification after regrouping is complete.

skills.name: Express final result
skills.definition: Write the computed result in acceptable final form by simplifying to lowest terms and, when needed, combining whole-number and fractional components into a single fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction or mixed number is reduced to lowest terms.
Tag when 0 over a denominator is rewritten as 0 or when a zero fractional part is absorbed into a whole number.
Tag when separate whole and fractional results are combined into one final answer form.
Tag when the solver explicitly states that the result is already in lowest terms as the final-answer step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag the arithmetic subtraction itself.
Do not tag preparatory rewriting of operands before subtraction.
Do not tag denominator matching or borrowing steps.
